selectionReason: The issue #60 rule selects up to ten absent Joyo kanji in frozen source-row order, with one support-word article per selected kanji. A qualifying support word uses JMdict news1, ichi1, spec1, or gai1; news2/spec2 do not qualify. The selected rows 135, 137, 139, 140, 146, 147, 148, 150, 152, and 153 are the first ten remaining Joyo rows after B158. Every support word's other kanji already has a card. Four rows take the rule's untagged route, each with a row-specific justification in its support mapping that must receive independent review: 又 (又聞き; the tagged 又 words are usually written in kana), 叔 (伯叔; the tags on 叔父 and 叔母 belong to the whole-word readings おじ and おば), 后 (太后; the tagged 皇后 and 皇太后 need 皇, which has no card), and 吏 (官吏; no 吏 word carries a qualifying tag, and 官吏 has only news2/spec2).

supportMappings.exceptionReason: Every candidate written with 又 that carries news1, ichi1, spec1, or gai1 in the pinned snapshot is a kana word: 又 また (entry 1524930, ichi1/news1) and 又は または (entry 1524990, ichi1/news1) are marked as usually written in kana, and the spec1 on またね (entry 2025400) belongs to the kana reading, with 又ね only a search-only kanji form. An article spelled 又 or 又は would teach a kanji spelling that JMdict marks as usually written in kana; B158 likewise kept 却って (かえ.って) and 即ち (すなわ.ち) for reference only for that reason. The untagged route of the issue #60 rule therefore applies, with a row-specific justification. 又聞き (entry 1584370) is untagged, and JMdict also lists the spelling また聞き. Its spellings and reading carry no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark; its other kanji 聞 has a card; and it backs the quizzed kun reading また-, the prefix that JMdict gives as sense 8 of 又 (“indirect”, see also 又聞き) and that Digital Daijisen illustrates with ―聞き and ―貸し. The alternatives are all untagged: 又貸し (1525120) uses the same prefix, and 又の名 (1524980) and 又の日 (1524970) are expressions that JMdict also lists with また in kana. Keep this explicit untagged exception for independent review.

No candidate qualifies through a reading of 叔. 叔父 (entry 1607070) and 叔母 (entry 1607100) carry ichi1/news1 only on the whole-word readings おじ and おば, which the Joyo table lists in its notes for 叔; their シュク readings しゅくふ and しゅくぼ are restricted to those spellings and untagged. This matches 伯父 and 伯母 for 伯 in B156, where 伯仲 was accepted. All other candidates written with 叔, including 叔世 and the おじ/おば compounds such as 大叔父 and 叔父さん, are untagged, so the untagged route of the issue #60 rule applies, with a row-specific justification. 伯叔 (entry 1474270) is the Joyo table's example for シュク; its other kanji 伯 has a card; its spelling and reading carry no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark; and it backs the quizzed on reading シュク. JMdict glosses it “brothers; one's father's brothers”. Keep this explicit untagged exception for independent review.

The candidates written with 后 that carry news1, ichi1, spec1, or gai1 cannot be used: 皇后 (entry 1280390, ichi1/news1) and 皇太后 (entry 1280450, news1) both need 皇, which has no card and is not in this batch; 午后 and 最后 are a rarely used and a search-only form of 午後 (1268990) and 最後 (1293810), whose tags belong to the 後 spellings; and 后 のち (1269330) lists 后 only as a search-only form. 后 きさき (1277320) carries only news2. The untagged route of the issue #60 rule therefore applies, with a row-specific justification. 太后 (entry 1787360) is untagged; its other kanji 太 has a card; its spelling and reading carry no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark; and it backs the quizzed on reading コウ, the only reading in the Joyo table. Its gloss, “empress dowager; queen mother”, names both an empress and a queen, and Digital Daijisen defines it as a title for 太皇太后 or 皇太后. The untagged alternatives include 王后 (2014540, “queen”), 母后 (1783060, “empress dowager”), 后妃 and 后宮. Keep this explicit untagged exception for independent review.

No candidate written with 吏 carries news1, ichi1, spec1, or gai1 in the pinned snapshot, so the untagged route of the issue #60 rule applies, with a row-specific justification. 官吏 (entry 1211850) is the only 吏 entry with any priority marker (news2/spec2, treated as untagged); all other 吏 entries, including 吏 り (1549690, archaic) and 吏員 (1549700), are untagged. 官吏 is the second example for リ in the Joyo table; its other kanji 官 has a card; its spelling and reading carry no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark, although JMdict marks its sense as dated; and it backs the quizzed on reading リ. JMdict glosses it “government official; public servant; civil servant”. 吏員 (“official”), the first Joyo example, and 能吏 (1470320), the third, are untagged. Keep this explicit untagged exception for independent review.
